summary: CyberLab v2 backend + frontend fully tested. All 9 pytest cases pass (plugins, rules, auto-decode powershell UTF-16LE chain, ransomware analyze with refang, run recipe hex/xor, IOC extract, nested base64, Mimikatz yara-lite). Frontend /cyberlab loads 3-pane UI; Auto Decode against pre-populated PS payload produces Clean verdict, Risk 8/100, 3 auto-generated recipe steps, decoded 'Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem' output, MITRE T1082 rendered. Ransomware Note example yields Malicious 100/100 with rules Ransomware_Note_Keywords + Shadow_Copy_Deletion and 3 IOCs. Palette add-op works. /detonate v1 unaffected. Navbar shows both Payload Lab and CyberLab v2.

issues: Top action buttons (Auto Decode / Run Recipe / Upload) sit at y~33px under sticky navbar — actionability check fails and Playwright needs force=true or JS .click(). Real users hover-clicking work fine, but consider adding scroll-margin-top or shifting action bar below navbar for polish.

action_items: (Nit) Add top padding / scroll-margin to CyberLab header action buttons so they aren't overlapped by sticky navbar.
critical_code_review_comments: CyberLab.jsx is ~560 lines — near threshold; consider extracting Palette, RecipePanel, AnalysisTabs into subcomponents once features grow.
All backend cyberlab modules use proper pydantic input models and return safe JSON (no _id leakage observed).
data-testid coverage is excellent across palette, recipe, output, tabs, IOCs, MITRE, rules — matches request spec.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 9 cyberlab pytest cases pass in <1s. Frontend requires JS .click() (page.evaluate) or force=true for top action buttons due to sticky navbar overlap. Example test IDs: example-Ransomware-Note, example-PowerShell--EncodedCommand. Ransomware auto-decode returns Malicious 100/100 with 3 rules & 3 IOCs.
